blocks.text: In order to provide the Zscaler Client Connector service, Zscaler has the right to process, use, reproduce, store, modify, and display the information from logs as defined in this article.
For Zscaler Client Connector, logs are defined as Packet Capture Logs, Client Connector Logs, and Tunnel Logs.

blocks.item: Packet Capture Logs: Packet capture logs of your transactions. You can globally enable or disable the packet capture. You have unlimited access to these logs and can delete them from a laptop, desktop, or personal mobile device.

Client Connector Logs: Client Connector logs capture information about the Zscaler Client Connector application and its usage on a given device. Log verbosity is configurable. Log information includes user interactions with the UI, for example, enabling and disabling services.

Tunnel Logs: Logs the status, operation, and errors related to tunneling. These logs include information about which data centers the client is connecting to, profile and policy downloads, and requests for specific domains or websites.

blocks.text: To enhance support for you and improve system performance analysis, logs might also contain local performance and diagnostic metrics, including technical and operational metrics related to agents, devices, and authentication (referred to as Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry). If your log tenant is located in the European Union, you can enable Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry from the settings page within the Zscaler Client Connector Portal. Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry is enabled by default for all others with the option to opt-out within the same settings page described earlier. To learn more, see Configuring Zscaler Client Connector App Profiles.
Your logs are stored in the same location as your Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) logs (in the United States, European Union, or Australia).

Zscaler retains log information for a rolling period of at least 90 days during the subscription term. When the subscription term ends or expires, the logs are deleted by Zscaler according to applicable retention cycles.
